 SALEM, Ore. (KATU) — With people getting new jobs for the coming holiday season, the Oregon Department of Human Services (DHS) says people should check their eligibility for food assistance benefits.
 DHS says seasonal employment, like working at a pumpkin patch or tree farm, or picking up extra hours during the holidays, could help people meet federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) rules.
 "Seasonal employment can be an opportunity to earn extra income while also helping people meet SNAP work or activity rules," said Jessica Amaya Hoffman, ODHS interim Oregon Eligibility Partnership Director. "If you've started a new job, picked up additional hours or are planning to work during the holidays, contact us. We can help you understand how your work and income affect your SNAP benefits and what steps you may need to take."
 Federal rules state that adults who are 18 to 64 years old have to have 80 hours of work or “qualifying activities” a month to keep getting their benefits, and getting a seasonal job can help people meet those requirements.
 State DHS officials encourage anyone who starts a new job or works more hours to report any changes, as it could impact their benefits.
